messages:
arjun: hi all, first-day setup. macbook pro arrived, followed setup assistant, but i got "Activation Lock" asking for the Apple ID I used during setup. i didn't realize i shouldn't sign in with personal iCloud. can someone advise? :cold_sweat:

it-bot: New device check: arjun-device-1773001234 logged. Activation Lock status: unknown.

itops: hey arjun, welcome! Activation Lock will block enrollment until the Apple ID is removed. quick question: did you see an option to 'Erase Mac' or did it stop at a login prompt asking for Apple ID?

arjun: it stopped at a screen "This Mac is linked to an Apple ID. Enter the Apple ID used to set up this device." i don't want to sign in with my personal account.

emma: no worries — we can handle this. two options: 1) if you can sign into your personal Apple ID and remove the Mac from iCloud (Devices -> remove), that clears it. 2) if not, we request Apple to remove Activation Lock via Apple Business Manager support — they'll ask for proof of purchase (we'll handle).

riley: can you DM me the serial from the sticker or run `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | awk -F': ' '/Serial/ {print $2}'` in Recovery Terminal? we'll check ABM and whether the vendor assigned it.

arjun: serial is C02YXY12345 (from box).

it-bot: ABM query: serial C02YXY12345 found in vendor-unassigned pool. Activation Lock status: associated with personal Apple ID.

itops: ok vendor didn't map it. i'll reassign the serial to our ABM profile and trigger a remote erase. that usually clears the temp state — but because it's stuck to a personal Apple ID we likely need Apple to remove the lock unless the account signs out. i'll start the Apple removal request.

emma: apple removal requests usually take 24-72 hours. if you want to get going sooner we can accept a temporary loaner or a device image in a VM; otherwise we'll queue the ABM+Apple flow. which would you prefer?

arjun: i'd prefer to wait if the loaner isn't immediate — fine to go through proper removal.

riley: requested Apple removal, uploaded proof of procurement and device serial. i've also assigned the serial to "Redwood Automated Enroll" in ABM and issued a remote erase as a precaution. you'll get a notification if the erase/assignment succeeds.

arjun: got a message "Remote erase initiated" on the Mac, it's erasing now. thanks.

it-bot: ABM update: serial C02YXY12345 assigned to Redwood Automated Enroll. Remote erase command issued. Apple removal request submitted (case #ABM-88921).

riley: after the wipe, come back to Setup Assistant and connect to Redwood-Secure. the device should present "This Mac is managed by Redwood Inference" and auto-enroll. if Activation Lock persists, we'll rely on Apple to clear it; they'll reply to the case.

arjun: back at setup, now shows "Managed by Redwood Inference" and enrollment proceeded. thanks all.

it-bot: Enrollment completed for arjun-device-1773001234. Profile: Redwood MDM (supervised). FileVault policy applied: pending.

emma: i'll approve FileVault to run and the recovery key will be stored in MDM. give it ~5 minutes then check `sudo fdesetup status`.

arjun: fdesetup status -> "FileVault is On." awesome. one last ask: do i get admin to install brew and devtools?

devex: yes, we grant temporary admin for 7 days. i've added you to the dev-installers group — you should be able to `brew install` and run Docker. run Rosetta if prompted: `/usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license`.

arjun: confirmed brew installs fine. appreciate the help everyone :tada:

itops: note for onboarding docs: remind new-hires to avoid signing into personal iCloud during Setup Assistant. we'll add a line and a short troubleshooting snippet for Activation Lock/ABM assignment.

emma: adding the doc update to the onboarding checklist (assign to devex).
